I used to be completely uninterested in cars and trucks. I've always owned pickup trucks for their utility and for pulling my boat but I've never cared about how they looked, the model, horsepower, etc. That all changed for me. In 2003 I bought a 2001 Ford F250 diesel pickup with 40,000 miles on it. At the time I didn't think much of it but diesel fuel was cheaper than gas back then. It's not pretty, or even a 4x4. I thought I'd keep it for a while then get another.

Then two things happened. The government implemented emission controls on new diesel trucks which forced the manufacturers to redesign their engines - which they did incredibly poorly. Suddenly I was the owner of one of the most sought-after trucks out there. After seeing I had the 7.3L diesel, people literally walked up to me and made me offers on the spot. I decided that since I had lucked into such a good truck I should try to keep it in better shape. The more I worked on it the better I got and it became more interesting and enjoyable for me. I'm to the point now that I do all maintenance and repair on the truck myself including transmission rebuilds, injector replacements, etc. Unless I break a piston there's nothing on that thing I can't fix myself.

The second thing that happened was I went over 100,000 miles on the engine. At that point I became infatuated with keeping the thing going - and still am. My goal is to keep it at least until 500,000 miles (I'm currently at 307,000). I constantly do modifications to improve the performance and longevity. I'm even active on some of the Ford truck forums such as www.powerstrokenation.com. My wife thinks I love that truck more than her. It's a close call on that one...

tl;dr - never interested in cars or trucks, then fell in love with one became a fanatic.
